defects.claim_says: The held text of EO 12608 does not name EO 10521 or any of its subjects; only its Section 2 (Bureau of the Budget) is tested
defects.source_says: EO 10521 Sec. 5 names the "Commissioner of Education of the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare"; EO 12608 Sec. 12 and Sec. 15 (catch-all for any order relating to functions delegated to HHS) substitute for "Health, Education, and Welfare"
defects.problem: the OFR note "Amended by: EO 12608" is not fully addressed; the HEW-substitution provisions, the likely basis of the note, and their effect (if any) on Section 5 are not analysed

evidence_checked: diff of genuine claim against the blind-review copy (only the planted dates differ)
scripted re-hash and quote-span check (all matched)
blind-review source reading carried over: held FR originals of the order and every acting order, OFR catalog notes, current-law mentions
reasoning: The genuine claim restores the Section 8(c) first_end date to 1959-03-13, which matches EO 10807 sec. 6(b)(3)(iii) and the signature date, so the planted defect is gone. The second defect found in blind review is independent of the plant and remains: the OFR catalog lists EO 12608 (1987-09-09) as amending EO 10521, and the claim explains it away by testing only EO 12608 Section 2 (Bureau of the Budget) and asserting that 12608 touches none of 10521's subjects. EO 10521 Section 5 refers to the Commissioner of Education of the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare, and EO 12608 Sections 12 and 15 substitute that department's name (Section 15 also in any other order relating to HHS functions). The claim must analyse whether Section 15 (or 12) reaches Section 5, record any wording event, and note the transfer of the Commissioner of Education's functions; until then the OFR note is not fully addressed.
